newsitem.title: USA: AMR Corp agreed to reduce Canadian fees.
newsitem.headline: AMR Corp agreed to reduce Canadian fees.

text.p: AMR Corp said Tuesday it will reduce its service fees to support Canadian Airlines Corp's restructuring plan.
AMR, the parent of American Airlines, said this support remains contingent on all parties, including all of Canadian Airlines' unions, supporting the restructuring plan.
While most of Calgary-based Canadian Airlines' unions agreed to support the survival plan, the Canadian Auto Workers union remains a major obstacle.
AMR holds a one-third economic interest in Canadian Airlines and a 25 percent voting interest.
AMR collects about $100 million annually from Canadian Airlines for computer technology and administrative services such as yield management, accounting, operations planning, and data processing.
AMR officials were not immediately available to comment on how much it would cut its fees or whether the fee reduction would affect its earnings.
